title: Empty message returns HTTP 200 instead of 422
expected_behavior: HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity with error message explaining the message field cannot be empty
actual_behavior: HTTP 200 OK with a generic chatbot response despite empty input
steps_to_reproduce: Observe HTTP 200 response with a generic reply
impact: Users can submit empty queries; chatbot wastes compute on meaningless requests
fix_suggestion: Add server-side validation: if message.strip() == '', return 422

title: Toxic content filter accepts 'kill' in a compound sentence

request_body.message: How do I kill boredom effectively?

response_body.response: I understand your query. Let me help you with that.

expected_behavior: Either: (a) HTTP 200 with a helpful response, OR (b) a smarter contextual filter that understands 'kill boredom' is benign
actual_behavior: HTTP 200 returned with a response — meaning the toxic filter MISSED this (a real harm filter would need NLP context)
steps_to_reproduce: POST /api/v1/chat with {"message": "How do I kill boredom?"}
Note the 200 response (filter should have reviewed context)
impact: False negatives in content moderation; basic keyword matching is insufficient for production
fix_suggestion: Replace simple keyword match with a context-aware NLP classifier

title: Feedback endpoint accepts rating=0 (out of range)
expected_behavior: HTTP 422 with error: rating must be between 1 and 5
impact: Data integrity issue; 0-star ratings corrupt average rating calculations
fix_suggestion: Change validation to: if rating not in range(1, 6): return 422

title: Response time spikes to >1s under minimal load
expected_behavior: P95 response time < 500ms under 50 concurrent users
actual_behavior: P95 response time was 1,240ms under 50 concurrent users
steps_to_reproduce: Run Locust with 50 users, 5 spawn rate
Observe P95 latency in the HTML report
impact: Poor user experience; SLA violation risk
fix_suggestion: Profile the route handler, move sleep() to async, add response caching
